task_1.title: Upgrade PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning to deprecation warning and introduce PytestReturnNotNoneWarning
task_1.description: PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning has been reclassified from a plain PytestWarning to a deprecation warning by changing its base class. A new intermediate warning class, PytestReturnNotNoneWarning, has been introduced in the public API as a parent for warnings related to test functions returning non-None values. Both PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning and PytestReturnNotNoneWarning now inherit from PytestRemovedIn8Warning, signaling that these conditions will become errors in pytest 8. This aligns unhandled coroutine warnings with the broader plan to treat non-None returns from test functions as errors in the next major release.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning is elevated from a general warning to a deprecation warning, signaling to users that unhandled coroutines in test functions will become hard errors in pytest 8. Introduce a new public warning class PytestReturnNotNoneWarning as the common ancestor for warnings about test functions returning non-None values, including unhandled coroutines.

expectation.grounded: PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning must inherit from PytestReturnNotNoneWarning, which itself inherits from PytestRemovedIn8Warning (a subclass of PytestDeprecationWarning). This means PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning is now an instance of DeprecationWarning, PytestDeprecationWarning, PytestRemovedIn8Warning, and PytestReturnNotNoneWarning. The new PytestReturnNotNoneWarning class must be exported as part of the public pytest namespace and included in __all__. PytestRemovedIn8Warning must no longer be marked as final so that it can be subclassed.
expectation.conceptual: When a test function yields an unhandled coroutine, the emitted warning should now be classified as a deprecation warning rather than a general warning. Users should be able to filter or catch this warning using standard Python deprecation warning categories. A new publicly accessible warning class for non-None test returns should serve as the shared base for all related warnings, providing a single filter point.

constraints.grounded: PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning must remain catchable by code that filters on PytestWarning, since PytestDeprecationWarning still inherits from PytestWarning. PytestReturnNotNoneWarning must be a subclass of PytestRemovedIn8Warning, not directly of PytestDeprecationWarning or PytestWarning. Existing warning filter configurations using PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning by exact class must continue to match. PytestRemovedIn8Warning must remain subclassable (not final).
constraints.conceptual: The reclassification must not break existing warning suppression or capture configurations that target the unhandled coroutine warning by its class name. The new warning hierarchy must preserve backward compatibility for users filtering on the general PytestWarning category. The deprecation pathway must clearly signal that these warnings will become errors in the next major version.

behavior: PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning is now a subclass of DeprecationWarning (via PytestReturnNotNoneWarning → PytestRemovedIn8Warning → PytestDeprecationWarning), so Python's default warning filters for DeprecationWarning will apply to it.
A new warning class PytestReturnNotNoneWarning is available in the public pytest namespace for filtering warnings about test functions returning non-None values.
isinstance checks against PytestDeprecationWarning, PytestRemovedIn8Warning, PytestReturnNotNoneWarning, and DeprecationWarning now return True for PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning instances.
PytestRemovedIn8Warning can now be subclassed by external code since the @final decorator has been removed.

Warning filters using -W or pytest.ini filterwarnings that match on DeprecationWarning will now also capture PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning, potentially changing visibility for users who previously only saw it under PytestWarning filters.
acceptance_criteria: When a test function returns an unhandled coroutine, the emitted warning should be an instance of PytestReturnNotNoneWarning and PytestDeprecationWarning.
When filtering warnings with simplefilter('ignore', DeprecationWarning), PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning should be suppressed.
When importing from the pytest namespace, PytestReturnNotNoneWarning should be accessible as pytest.PytestReturnNotNoneWarning.
When checking issubclass(PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning, PytestRemovedIn8Warning), the result should be True.
When checking issubclass(PytestReturnNotNoneWarning, PytestRemovedIn8Warning), the result should be True.
When existing code filters warnings using filterwarnings('ignore', category=PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning), the filter should still correctly suppress these warnings.
When subclassing PytestRemovedIn8Warning from external code, no error should be raised (the class is no longer final).

task_3.title: Deprecate legacy attribute/mark-based hook configuration in favor of pytest.hookimpl and pytest.hookspec decorators
task_3.description: Previously, pytest silently supported configuring hook implementations and specifications via function attributes (e.g., setting tryfirst as an attribute on the function) or pytest marks (e.g., @pytest.mark.tryfirst). This update deprecates those legacy mechanisms and emits PytestDeprecationWarning when they are detected, directing users to migrate to the explicit pytest.hookimpl() and pytest.hookspec() decorator APIs. The deprecation warning is location-aware, pointing to the exact function definition. When warnings are promoted to errors, the location information is preserved in the raised exception message.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that hook implementation and hook specification functions configured via legacy mechanisms (function attributes or pytest marks such as tryfirst, trylast, optionalhook, hookwrapper, firstresult, historic) emit a PytestDeprecationWarning at runtime, guiding users to migrate to the pytest.hookimpl() and pytest.hookspec() decorator APIs. The legacy configuration must continue to function (the options must still take effect) but must no longer be silently accepted.

expectation.grounded: When PytestPluginManager.parse_hookimpl_opts encounters a pytest_-prefixed method that was not decorated with pytest.hookimpl but carries legacy attributes or pytestmark entries for tryfirst, trylast, optionalhook, or hookwrapper, it must emit a PytestDeprecationWarning of type HOOK_LEGACY_MARKING via warn_explicit_for, referencing the method's qualified name and the detected options. The same applies to parse_hookspec_opts for firstresult and historic options. The standard pluggy-based parse_hookimpl_opts result takes precedence; legacy detection only fires as a fallback for pytest_-prefixed routines without explicit hookimpl decoration. The warning must be issued at the source location of the hook function definition (file and line number). When warnings are configured as errors, the raised exception must include the file path and line number in its message.
expectation.conceptual: Any hook function relying on the old attribute-based or mark-based configuration approach must produce a deprecation warning at plugin registration time. The warning must clearly identify the affected function, the legacy options detected, and the recommended decorator replacement. Hooks decorated with the modern pytest.hookimpl or pytest.hookspec APIs must not trigger any deprecation warning. The legacy options must still be honored functionally during the deprecation period.

constraints.grounded: Hooks that are already decorated with pytest.hookimpl() must not trigger legacy detection or deprecation warnings; the pluggy-parsed result short-circuits the legacy path. Only callable routines (as determined by inspect.isroutine) are considered for legacy hook detection. The tryfirst and trylast marker help-text descriptions must include a DEPRECATED notice referencing the decorator alternative. The HOOK_LEGACY_MARKING warning must be an UnformattedWarning wrapping PytestDeprecationWarning. Non-pytest_-prefixed methods must not be processed through the legacy path.
constraints.conceptual: The deprecation must not break existing plugins that use the legacy approach; their hook options must still take effect. Only functions following the pytest_ naming convention should be subject to legacy detection. Modern decorator-based hooks must be completely unaffected. The deprecation messaging must direct users to the official migration documentation.

behavior: When a hook implementation function uses a legacy attribute (e.g., function.tryfirst = True) or a pytest mark (e.g., @pytest.mark.tryfirst) instead of @pytest.hookimpl(tryfirst=True), a PytestDeprecationWarning is emitted at the function's definition location.

When a hook specification function uses a legacy attribute or mark for firstresult or historic instead of @pytest.hookspec(), a PytestDeprecationWarning is emitted at the function's definition location.
The deprecation warning message identifies the hook type (impl or spec), the function's qualified name, and the specific legacy options that were detected.

If pluggy's standard parse_hookimpl_opts already returns a result (i.e., the function is properly decorated with pytest.hookimpl), the legacy fallback path is skipped entirely and no warning is issued.
Only actual routines (as verified by inspect.isroutine) are considered for legacy hook detection; non-callable attributes are ignored.
When warnings are configured as errors (e.g., -W error::PytestDeprecationWarning), the raised exception preserves the file and line number of the offending hook definition in its message.
The marker help text for tryfirst and trylast now includes a DEPRECATED notice directing users to the decorator-based alternative.
acceptance_criteria: When a plugin defines a pytest_-prefixed hook implementation with a legacy attribute (e.g., func.trylast = True) and no @pytest.hookimpl decorator, a PytestDeprecationWarning should be raised containing the function's qualified name and the detected option.

When a plugin defines a pytest_-prefixed hook implementation with a pytest mark (e.g., @pytest.mark.hookwrapper) and no @pytest.hookimpl decorator, a PytestDeprecationWarning should be raised containing the function's qualified name and the detected option.
When a hook specification uses a legacy attribute or mark for firstresult or historic instead of @pytest.hookspec, a PytestDeprecationWarning should be raised.
When a hook implementation is properly decorated with @pytest.hookimpl(), no deprecation warning should be emitted regardless of any additional legacy attributes or marks present.
When running with -W error::PytestDeprecationWarning, the raised exception message should include the file path and line number where the legacy-configured hook is defined.
Given a plugin method that does not start with pytest_, it should never trigger legacy hook detection or deprecation warnings.
Given a plugin attribute that is not a callable routine, it should not be processed through the legacy hook detection path.
The legacy hook options (tryfirst, trylast, optionalhook, hookwrapper, firstresult, historic) must still be functionally honored during the deprecation period even when the warning is emitted.

task_2.title: Remove py library dependency by vendoring py.path and py.error
task_2.description: pytest removes its hard dependency on the external py library by vendoring internal copies of py.path and py.error. A shim module ensures that code importing py.path or py.error continues to work transparently. When the py library is installed it takes precedence over the vendored copies. The sysexec method on LocalPath now raises RuntimeError on non-zero exit codes instead of the former py.process.cmdexec specialized exception.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest no longer requires the py library as an install-time dependency. Ensure that vendored copies of py.path and py.error are provided so that existing code referencing these modules continues to work. Ensure that if the py library is separately installed, it takes precedence over the vendored copies. Ensure that LocalPath.sysexec raises RuntimeError instead of the former py.process.cmdexec error when a subprocess exits with a non-zero return code.

expectation.grounded: After upgrading, pytest must not declare py as a required dependency. Importing py.path and py.error must resolve to vendored modules within _pytest._py when the py library is not installed. When the py library is installed, its py.path and py.error modules must take precedence over the vendored shim. LocalPath (py.path.local) must remain fully functional including all filesystem operations, path manipulation, and module importing. LocalPath.sysexec must raise RuntimeError (not py.process.cmdexec.Error) when the invoked process returns a non-zero exit code. The Error class hierarchy in the vendored py.error module must preserve errno-based exception subclassing (e.g., ENOENT, EEXIST, EACCES) and the checked_call utility.
expectation.conceptual: pytest should install and run without the py library present. All existing uses of py.path and py.error should continue to resolve correctly. The local path object should behave identically to its predecessor for all filesystem, import, and path-manipulation operations. The only observable behavioral change is that sysexec raises a standard RuntimeError instead of a library-specific process execution error.

constraints.grounded: No other py.* modules beyond py.path and py.error are vendored; code depending on other py submodules (e.g., py.process, py.io) must still install the py library separately. The vendored error module must preserve the ErrorMaker pattern that dynamically creates errno-specific exception classes inheriting from Error (itself an EnvironmentError subclass). The shim module must register vendored modules in sys.modules under the keys py.error and py.path. The shim must be bypassed when py/__init__.py exists on the import path.
constraints.conceptual: Only py.path and py.error are replaced; other py submodules are not covered. Backward compatibility for py.path and py.error must be maintained without requiring users to change their imports. The vendored modules must coexist gracefully with a fully installed py library when present.

behavior: pytest installs and runs without the py library in the environment
Importing py.path resolves to the vendored _pytest._py.path module when py is not installed
Importing py.error resolves to the vendored _pytest._py.error module when py is not installed
When the py library is installed, its modules take precedence over the vendored shim
LocalPath.sysexec raises RuntimeError (with return code, command path, stdout, and stderr) when a subprocess exits with non-zero status
LocalPath.sysexec no longer raises py.process.cmdexec.Error
The vendored error module dynamically generates errno-specific exception classes (ENOENT, EEXIST, EACCES, etc.) that subclass EnvironmentError
All LocalPath filesystem operations (join, listdir, stat, remove, copy, rename, ensure, etc.) continue to function using the vendored error.checked_call mechanism
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is installed in a clean environment without the py library, importing pytest succeeds without ImportError
When py is not installed, importing py.path returns the vendored path module and py.path.local is usable
When py is not installed, importing py.error returns the vendored error module with errno-based exception classes
When the py library is installed alongside pytest, importing py.path and py.error returns the py library's own modules rather than the vendored copies
When LocalPath.sysexec is called with an executable that exits with a non-zero return code, it raises RuntimeError
When LocalPath.sysexec is called with an executable that exits with a non-zero return code, the RuntimeError does not inherit from or reference py.process.cmdexec
When LocalPath.sysexec is called with an executable that exits successfully, it returns the stdout output as a string
When code uses py.path.local for filesystem operations (creating, reading, writing, removing files and directories), all operations behave identically to the previous py library version
When code catches error.ENOENT or other errno-specific exceptions from the vendored error module, the exception hierarchy is preserved and catching EnvironmentError also catches them

task_5.title: Deprecation warning for test functions returning non-None values
task_5.description: Pytest now emits a deprecation warning when a test function returns a value other than None. This addresses a common beginner mistake where users write 'return expr == expected' instead of 'assert expr == expected', which silently produces false-positive passing tests. The warning is classified as a PytestRemovedIn8Warning, signaling that returning non-None from tests will become a hard error in pytest 8.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when a test function returns a value other than None, pytest emits a deprecation warning alerting the user that they likely intended to use `assert` instead of `return`. This catches a common mistake where tests silently pass because a boolean expression is returned rather than asserted, producing false positives in test suites.

expectation.grounded: When pytest_pyfunc_call executes a test function and the return value is not None, a PytestReturnNotNoneWarning (subclass of PytestRemovedIn8Warning and PytestDeprecationWarning) must be emitted via the warnings module. The warning message must include the test node ID and the repr of the returned value, and must indicate this will become an error in a future version of pytest. The check must not interfere with the existing async coroutine/iterator detection path, which should continue to trigger async_warn_and_skip as before.
expectation.conceptual: When a test function returns any value other than None, pytest should issue a visible deprecation warning suggesting the user likely meant to assert the expression rather than return it. The warning should clearly identify which test produced it and what value was returned, and should communicate that this behavior will become a hard error in a future major version.

constraints.grounded: The new PytestReturnNotNoneWarning must be a subclass of PytestRemovedIn8Warning, which itself is a subclass of PytestDeprecationWarning. The warning must only fire when the result is not None; a test returning None explicitly or implicitly must not trigger the warning. The existing detection of coroutines and async iterators via __await__ and __aiter__ must remain unaffected and take precedence over the non-None return check. The new warning class must be exposed under the pytest module namespace (__module__ = 'pytest').
constraints.conceptual: Tests that return None (explicitly or by falling through without a return statement) must continue to pass silently with no new warnings. Async test detection must not be disrupted. The warning must be a standard Python deprecation warning so that users can filter, capture, or suppress it using standard warning filter mechanisms.

behavior: A new warning class PytestReturnNotNoneWarning is introduced as a subclass of PytestRemovedIn8Warning.
After a test function executes and its return value is not None and not an async coroutine/iterator, a PytestReturnNotNoneWarning is emitted.
The warning message includes the test's node ID, the repr of the returned value, and a suggestion to use assert instead of return.
The warning indicates this will become an error in a future version of pytest.
Tests returning None (implicitly or explicitly) produce no such warning.
Async test functions returning coroutines or async iterators continue to be handled by the existing async_warn_and_skip path, not the new non-None return check.
The @final decorator is removed from PytestRemovedIn8Warning to allow subclassing by PytestReturnNotNoneWarning.
acceptance_criteria: When a test function returns a non-None value (e.g., a boolean from 'return a == b'), a PytestReturnNotNoneWarning is emitted during test execution.
When a test function returns None or has no explicit return statement, no PytestReturnNotNoneWarning is emitted.
When an async test function returns a coroutine or async iterator, the existing async warning/skip behavior is triggered instead of PytestReturnNotNoneWarning.
The emitted warning is an instance of PytestReturnNotNoneWarning, which is a subclass of PytestRemovedIn8Warning and PytestDeprecationWarning.
The warning message identifies the specific test (by node ID) and displays the returned value.
The warning can be captured, filtered, or converted to an error using standard Python warning filters (e.g., -W error::pytest.PytestReturnNotNoneWarning).
Existing test suites that do not return non-None values from tests see no behavioral change.

task_4.title: Deprecate nose test support with runtime warnings
task_4.description: Pytest's built-in support for running tests written for the nose framework has been officially deprecated. When nose-style setup/teardown functions or methods are encountered during test collection and execution, pytest now emits PytestRemovedIn8Warning deprecation warnings. This affects plain setup() and teardown() functions at the module and function level, nose-style setup(self) and teardown(self) methods on test classes (instead of the pytest-idiomatic setup_method/teardown_method), and usage of the @with_setup decorator. The nose test runner has been in maintenance-only mode for years, and this deprecation signals the eventual removal of nose compatibility from pytest's core in a future major version.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement:
Ensure that pytest emits deprecation warnings when nose-style test setup and teardown patterns are used, signaling that nose support will be removed in a future release. Specifically:
- Ensure that plain setup() and teardown() functions invoked through the nose plugin trigger a PytestRemovedIn8Warning.
- Ensure that class-level setup(self) and teardown(self) methods (nose idioms) trigger a PytestRemovedIn8Warning advising the user to rename them to setup_method(self) and teardown_method(self).
- Ensure that the @with_setup decorator usage is covered by the deprecation notice.
- Ensure that the deprecation warnings include the node ID of the offending test and the name of the deprecated method, along with a link to the deprecation documentation.

expectation.grounded: When the nose plugin is active and call_optional invokes a nose-style setup or teardown function on a test item, a PytestRemovedIn8Warning (via the NOSE_SUPPORT warning constant) must be emitted, including the test's nodeid, the method name, and the stage (setup or teardown). When Class collection detects that a test class defines setup(self) or teardown(self) instead of setup_method(self) or teardown_method(self), and the nose plugin is loaded, a PytestRemovedIn8Warning (via the NOSE_SUPPORT_METHOD warning constant) must be emitted, including the nodeid and the method name, with guidance to rename the method to the _method variant. Standard pytest setup_method/teardown_method and module-level pytest fixtures must not trigger any nose deprecation warning.
expectation.conceptual: When tests rely on nose-specific setup and teardown conventions, pytest must warn users at runtime that this support is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. The warnings must clearly identify which test and which method triggered the deprecation, and must provide actionable guidance for migrating to standard pytest idioms. Tests that already use pytest-native setup/teardown patterns must remain unaffected.

constraints.grounded: The nose plugin must remain functional — nose-style setup and teardown methods must still be invoked as before, with the deprecation warning emitted in addition to (not instead of) the existing behavior. The warnings must be of type PytestRemovedIn8Warning so they are filterable via standard warning filters. The NOSE_SUPPORT_METHOD warning must only be emitted when the nose plugin is actually loaded (has_plugin check). Existing test suites that use setup_method/teardown_method must produce no new warnings.
constraints.conceptual: Nose-style tests must continue to pass and function correctly during the deprecation period — only warnings are added, not behavioral changes. The deprecation warnings must be filterable so that users can suppress them if needed. No false positives should occur for tests using standard pytest conventions.

behavior: When a nose-style setup() or teardown() function is found on a test object during pytest_runtest_setup and invoked via call_optional, a PytestRemovedIn8Warning is emitted before the method executes, containing the test nodeid, method name, and stage.

When a test class defines setup(self) instead of setup_method(self) and the nose plugin is loaded, the class collector falls back to the nose-style name and emits a PytestRemovedIn8Warning after invoking setup, advising the user to rename to setup_method(self).

When a test class defines teardown(self) instead of teardown_method(self) and the nose plugin is loaded, the class collector falls back to the nose-style name and emits a PytestRemovedIn8Warning after invoking teardown, advising the user to rename to teardown_method(self).
If a test class already defines setup_method or teardown_method, the nose fallback path is not triggered and no deprecation warning is emitted.
The warnings reference the official deprecation documentation URL for nose support removal.
Test suites running with -W error::PytestRemovedIn8Warning will fail when nose-style patterns are detected, providing a strict migration enforcement path.
acceptance_criteria: When a module-level test function uses a nose-style setup() function (not a pytest fixture), running pytest should produce a PytestRemovedIn8Warning mentioning the test's nodeid and the method name.
When a module-level test function uses a nose-style teardown() function, running pytest should produce a PytestRemovedIn8Warning mentioning the test's nodeid and the method name.
When a test class defines setup(self) but not setup_method(self), and the nose plugin is active, running pytest should produce a PytestRemovedIn8Warning advising to rename setup to setup_method.

When a test class defines teardown(self) but not teardown_method(self), and the nose plugin is active, running pytest should produce a PytestRemovedIn8Warning advising to rename teardown to teardown_method.
When a test class defines setup_method(self) and/or teardown_method(self), no nose deprecation warning should be emitted regardless of whether the nose plugin is loaded.
When the nose plugin is not loaded, class-level setup(self) and teardown(self) methods should not trigger any NOSE_SUPPORT_METHOD warning.
All emitted nose deprecation warnings should be of type PytestRemovedIn8Warning and should be suppressible via standard Python warning filters.
All emitted warnings should include a documentation URL pointing to the nose deprecation guidance.

task_6.title: Add shell-style wildcard (glob) support to testpaths configuration
task_6.description: The testpaths configuration value now supports shell-style wildcard patterns (e.g. src/*/tests), which are expanded via glob before test collection. This is especially useful for monorepos with hierarchical directory structures. Additionally, a new public Config.ArgsSource enum and Config.args_source attribute were introduced to explicitly track where test arguments originated (command line, invocation directory, or testpaths config). The terminal header logic that decides whether to display testpaths was updated to use this new source attribute instead of the previous fragile heuristic that compared argument values directly.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the testpaths configuration option accepts shell-style wildcard patterns (e.g. src/*/tests) and correctly expands them to matching directories during test collection. Ensure that a new public Config.ArgsSource enum and Config.args_source attribute are available to indicate whether test arguments were sourced from the command line, the invocation directory, or the testpaths configuration value. Ensure that the terminal header accurately displays testpaths information by using the new args_source attribute rather than a value-comparison heuristic.

expectation.grounded: When testpaths contains glob patterns (e.g. 'src/*/tests'), Config.parse() should expand them using recursive glob matching and collect all matching paths in sorted order. When pyargs mode is active, testpaths values should be passed through without glob expansion. A new Config.ArgsSource enum should be defined with members ARGS, INCOVATION_DIR, and TESTPATHS. After parsing, Config.args_source should be set to ArgsSource.ARGS if explicit command-line arguments were provided, ArgsSource.TESTPATHS if arguments were resolved from the testpaths config, or ArgsSource.INCOVATION_DIR if the invocation directory was used as a fallback. The TerminalReporter should display the testpaths line in the header when Config.args_source equals ArgsSource.TESTPATHS.
expectation.conceptual: Wildcard patterns in the testpaths configuration should be transparently expanded to their matching filesystem paths before test collection begins. The framework should track the origin of test arguments via a public enumeration on the Config object, distinguishing between explicit command-line arguments, the testpaths configuration, and the invocation directory fallback. The terminal session header should reliably report when testpaths are in effect based on the tracked argument source, not by comparing argument values.

constraints.grounded: Existing testpaths configurations without wildcards must continue to work identically. The Config.ArgsSource enum must be publicly accessible as Config.ArgsSource. When pyargs mode is enabled, glob expansion must not be applied to testpaths entries. If glob expansion of testpaths yields no matches, the fallback to invocation directory must still occur. The args_source attribute must be set on Config after parse completes.
constraints.conceptual: Backward compatibility with non-wildcard testpaths values must be preserved. Module-style test path resolution (pyargs) must not be affected by glob expansion. The fallback behavior when no test paths are resolved must remain unchanged. The new argument-source tracking must not alter existing test collection semantics beyond enabling wildcard expansion.

behavior: Glob patterns in testpaths (e.g. 'src/*/tests', 'tests/**/unit') are expanded to matching filesystem paths in sorted order during argument parsing.
A new Config.ArgsSource enum is exposed with members ARGS, INCOVATION_DIR, and TESTPATHS.
Config.args_source is set to ArgsSource.ARGS when explicit command-line arguments are provided.
Config.args_source is set to ArgsSource.TESTPATHS when arguments are resolved from the testpaths configuration value.
Config.args_source is set to ArgsSource.INCOVATION_DIR when the invocation directory is used as a fallback.
When pyargs mode is active, testpaths entries are used as-is without glob expansion.
The terminal header displays the testpaths line if and only if Config.args_source is ArgsSource.TESTPATHS, replacing the old heuristic comparison.
If testpaths glob patterns match no paths, the system falls back to using the invocation directory.
acceptance_criteria: When testpaths is set to 'src/*/tests' and matching directories exist, running pytest without explicit arguments should collect tests from all matching directories in sorted order.
When testpaths contains a non-wildcard path like 'tests/', behavior should be identical to previous versions.
When explicit test arguments are provided on the command line, Config.args_source should equal ArgsSource.ARGS regardless of testpaths configuration.
When testpaths is used and the invocation directory equals the root path, Config.args_source should equal ArgsSource.TESTPATHS.
When no explicit arguments are given and testpaths is empty or yields no glob matches, Config.args_source should equal ArgsSource.INCOVATION_DIR and the invocation directory should be used.
When pyargs mode is enabled, testpaths entries should not undergo glob expansion.
The terminal session header should display 'testpaths: ...' only when args_source is ArgsSource.TESTPATHS, not based on argument value comparison.
Config.ArgsSource should be accessible as a public enum on the Config class with members ARGS, INCOVATION_DIR, and TESTPATHS.

task_7.title: Broaden parametrize argnames to accept any Sequence[str]
task_7.description: The argnames parameter of @pytest.mark.parametrize() and related internal APIs has been widened from accepting only str, list[str], or tuple[str, ...] to accepting any Sequence[str]. Previously, any value that was not a list or tuple was assumed to be a string and split by commas; now, only actual str instances undergo comma splitting, allowing other sequence types (e.g., custom sequences, deques, generator-backed sequences) to be passed directly as argument name collections.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that @pytest.mark.parametrize() accepts any Sequence[str] (not just list or tuple) as the argnames parameter, while preserving the existing behavior of treating a plain str as a comma-delimited name list.

expectation.grounded: The argnames parameter of Metafunc.parametrize(), ParameterSet._parse_parametrize_args(), ParameterSet._for_parametrize(), and the _ParametrizeMarkDecorator.__call__() type stub should accept Union[str, Sequence[str]]. When argnames is a str, it should be split on commas with whitespace stripped, as before. When argnames is any non-str Sequence[str] (e.g., a custom Sequence implementation, a deque, a KeysView, etc.), it should be used directly without comma splitting. Return types from _parse_parametrize_args and _for_parametrize should reflect Sequence[str] rather than Union[List[str], Tuple[str, ...]].
expectation.conceptual: When a user passes any sequence-like collection of strings (beyond just list or tuple) as argument names to parametrize, the framework should accept it and use those names directly. Only when a bare string is provided should the framework perform comma-based splitting to extract individual argument names. The type annotations should reflect this broader acceptance.

constraints.grounded: Passing a str to argnames must still trigger comma-delimited parsing and whitespace stripping, preserving backward compatibility. Passing a list[str] or tuple[str, ...] must continue to work identically as before. The isinstance check must target str specifically, not use a negated check against list/tuple, to correctly handle arbitrary Sequence[str] subtypes. The force_tuple flag logic (single-element detection) must only apply to the str-splitting code path.
constraints.conceptual: Existing tests and user code that pass str, list, or tuple as argnames must not break. The change must not alter how string-based argument names are parsed. Only the dispatch logic (which types trigger comma splitting vs. direct use) changes, and it must correctly distinguish strings from all other sequence types.

behavior: When argnames is a str, it is split on commas with each element stripped of whitespace, and force_tuple is set to True when only one name results — unchanged from prior behavior.
When argnames is a list[str] or tuple[str, ...], it is passed through directly without splitting — unchanged from prior behavior.

When argnames is any other Sequence[str] (e.g., a custom Sequence subclass, collections.deque, or similar), it is now passed through directly without comma splitting, whereas previously it would have been incorrectly treated as a string and split.
The type annotations for argnames in all public and internal APIs are broadened from Union[str, List[str], Tuple[str, ...]] to Union[str, Sequence[str]].
The return type annotations of _parse_parametrize_args and _for_parametrize are broadened from Union[List[str], Tuple[str, ...]] to Sequence[str].
acceptance_criteria: When argnames is a plain str like 'a, b, c', it should be split into ['a', 'b', 'c'] — existing behavior preserved.
When argnames is a list like ['x', 'y'], it should be used directly without splitting — existing behavior preserved.
When argnames is a tuple like ('x', 'y'), it should be used directly without splitting — existing behavior preserved.

When argnames is a non-list, non-tuple Sequence[str] (e.g., a custom Sequence subclass containing ['a', 'b']), it should be accepted and used directly as argument names without comma splitting or errors.
When argnames is a single-element str like 'a', force_tuple should be True, ensuring single-parameter values are wrapped correctly — existing behavior preserved.
When argnames is a non-str Sequence with a single element like deque(['a']), force_tuple should be False, matching existing list/tuple behavior for single-element collections.
Static type checkers should accept any Sequence[str] (including custom implementations) passed to @pytest.mark.parametrize() argnames without type errors.

task_8.title: Add --no-showlocals flag to override --showlocals from addopts
task_8.description: When --showlocals is declared globally via addopts in pytest configuration, there is no way to suppress local variable display for individual test runs or CI steps. A new --no-showlocals command-line flag is introduced that negates the effect of --showlocals, allowing per-invocation overrides of the global setting.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can override a globally configured --showlocals option on a per-invocation basis. When --showlocals is set in addopts (e.g., in pyproject.toml or pytest.ini), it is currently impossible to disable local variable display for a specific test run without modifying the configuration file. A --no-showlocals flag should be provided so that CLI invocations can negate the global setting.

expectation.grounded: A new --no-showlocals option is registered via pytest_addoption on the terminal reporting option group. It uses action='store_false' and shares the same dest='showlocals' as --showlocals, so the last flag specified on the combined (addopts + CLI) argument list determines the final value. When --no-showlocals is the last flag, config.option.showlocals resolves to False, and traceback representations omit local variables. The option should appear in pytest --help output with a description indicating it negates --showlocals passed through addopts.
expectation.conceptual: When a user passes --no-showlocals on the command line, local variable display in tracebacks is suppressed, even if --showlocals was previously enabled via addopts or earlier arguments. The two flags (--showlocals and --no-showlocals) act as a toggle pair: whichever appears last in the effective argument list wins.

constraints.grounded: The default behavior of --showlocals must remain unchanged (disabled by default). Passing --showlocals alone (without addopts conflict) must continue to show locals in tracebacks. The --no-showlocals flag must only affect the showlocals configuration dest and must not interfere with other traceback-related options such as --tb. Existing test suites that do not use --no-showlocals must see no change in behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The addition of --no-showlocals must be purely additive and must not alter existing default behavior. Tests that rely on --showlocals being enabled globally should still work unless --no-showlocals is explicitly passed. No other traceback formatting behavior should be affected.

behavior: A new --no-showlocals CLI option is available in pytest's terminal reporting option group.
When --no-showlocals is passed, config.option.showlocals is set to False regardless of prior --showlocals flags.
When addopts contains --showlocals and the CLI includes --no-showlocals, local variables are hidden from tracebacks because --no-showlocals appears later in argument parsing order.
When neither --showlocals nor --no-showlocals is passed, the default behavior remains: locals are not shown in tracebacks.
When --showlocals is passed without --no-showlocals, locals continue to be displayed in tracebacks as before.
The --no-showlocals flag is visible in pytest --help output under the terminal reporting group.
acceptance_criteria: When --no-showlocals is passed on the CLI, tracebacks should not include local variable listings.
When addopts is configured with --showlocals and the user invokes pytest with --no-showlocals, tracebacks should not display local variables.
When --showlocals is passed without --no-showlocals, tracebacks should display local variables as before.
When neither flag is passed, the default behavior (no locals shown) is preserved.
Running pytest --help should list --no-showlocals with a description indicating it negates --showlocals from addopts.
When --showlocals appears after --no-showlocals in the argument list, locals should be shown (last-flag-wins semantics).

task_9.title: Improve assertion messages for Unicode-normalized string comparisons
task_9.description: When two strings that differ only in Unicode normalization form (e.g., NFC vs NFD) are compared in an assertion, they render identically in the failure output, making the error message confusing and unhelpful. This change detects when both operands are strings whose NFD normalizations are equal and switches to an ASCII-escaped representation so that the underlying codepoint differences become visible to the user.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when an assertion compares two strings that are visually identical but differ in Unicode normalization form (e.g., NFC vs NFD), the assertion failure message clearly reveals the difference rather than displaying two identical-looking strings. Previously, users saw output like `assert 'hyvä' == 'hyvä'` with no visible distinction, making it impossible to diagnose the mismatch from the error output alone.

expectation.grounded: The `assertrepr_compare` function must accept a `use_ascii` parameter (defaulting to False). When both `left` and `right` are `str` instances and `unicodedata.normalize('NFD', left) == unicodedata.normalize('NFD', right)`, the function must set `use_ascii` to True. When `use_ascii` is True, the `saferepr` and `saferepr_unlimited` callables must be invoked with `use_ascii=True`, causing non-ASCII and combining characters to be rendered as escaped codepoints (ASCII representation). In verbose mode (verbose > 1), `saferepr_unlimited` must be used instead of the former `safeformat` function.
expectation.conceptual: When a string equality assertion fails and both strings normalize to the same Unicode form, the assertion output must use an ASCII-safe representation that makes invisible codepoint-level differences (such as precomposed vs decomposed characters) visible to the user. In all other cases, the existing human-readable representation must be preserved unchanged.

constraints.grounded: The `use_ascii` detection must only activate when both operands are `str` type and their NFD normalizations are equal. The `use_ascii` flag must not alter representation for non-string comparisons or for string comparisons that do not normalize to the same NFD form. The `saferepr` maxsize truncation behavior must be preserved in non-verbose mode. The switch from `safeformat` to `saferepr_unlimited` must only apply in verbose mode (verbose > 1).
constraints.conceptual: The improved representation must only apply to the specific case of Unicode-normalization-equivalent strings. All other assertion failure messages, including those for non-string types and for strings that differ beyond normalization, must remain unchanged. Truncation behavior for long strings in non-verbose mode must be preserved.

behavior: When both sides of a string equality assertion are str instances and their NFD normalizations are equal, the assertion diff output uses ASCII-escaped representation to surface codepoint differences.
When comparing strings that do not NFD-normalize to the same value, the assertion diff output continues to use the standard human-readable representation.
When comparing non-string types, assertion output is completely unaffected by this change.

In verbose mode (verbose > 1), the unlimited-length safe representation function is used instead of the former format function, with ASCII escaping applied when Unicode normalization equivalence is detected.
In normal verbosity mode, the maxsize-bounded safe representation is used with ASCII escaping applied when Unicode normalization equivalence is detected.
acceptance_criteria: When asserting equality of a string in NFC form against the same string in NFD form (e.g., 'hyv\xe4' vs 'hyva\u0308'), the failure message must display escaped codepoint representations that visually differ, rather than two identical-looking rendered strings.
When asserting equality of two strings that differ in content (not just normalization), the failure message must use the standard repr-based display without ASCII escaping.
When asserting equality of non-string values, the failure output must be unchanged from prior behavior.
When running with verbose > 1, the full (non-truncated) representation must be shown with ASCII escaping applied for normalization-equivalent string pairs.
When running at default verbosity, the maxsize-truncated representation must be shown with ASCII escaping applied for normalization-equivalent string pairs.

Given two strings 'hyv\xe4' (NFC) and 'hyva\u0308' (NFD), when they are compared in an assert statement, then the assertion error output must show distinguishable representations revealing the different codepoints.

task_12.title: Use stdlib tomllib for TOML parsing on Python 3.11+
task_12.description: On Python 3.11 and above, pytest now uses the standard library's tomllib module to parse TOML configuration files (e.g., pyproject.toml) instead of the third-party tomli package. On earlier Python versions, tomli remains in use. This reduces the external dependency footprint for users running Python 3.11+, with no change in observable TOML parsing behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest uses the standard library's tomllib module for TOML parsing when running on Python 3.11 or later, removing the need for the third-party tomli dependency on those versions. On Python versions below 3.11, ensure that the existing tomli dependency continues to be used for TOML parsing with no behavioral change.

expectation.grounded: When running on Python >= 3.11, the TOML configuration loading path (load_config_dict_from_file) must import and use tomllib from the standard library. When running on Python < 3.11, it must import tomli (aliased as tomllib). In both cases, TOML content is parsed via tomllib.loads(), and any malformed TOML must raise tomllib.TOMLDecodeError, which is caught and re-raised as UsageError. The tomli package must not appear as a required dependency for Python >= 3.11 environments.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should automatically select the appropriate TOML parsing backend based on the Python version at runtime. Users on Python 3.11+ should not need the tomli package installed. Users on earlier Python versions should see no change. TOML parsing errors should continue to be reported as UsageError regardless of the backend.

constraints.grounded: On Python < 3.11, tomli must remain a required dependency and must be used for TOML parsing. The TOMLDecodeError exception handling must work identically regardless of which backend is active. The UsageError wrapping of TOML parse failures must remain intact. The public configuration loading API must not change its return types or signatures.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not alter any user-observable TOML parsing behavior, error reporting, or configuration loading outcomes. The only difference is which underlying library provides the TOML parser. Backward compatibility with Python versions below 3.11 must be preserved.

behavior: On Python >= 3.11, the standard library tomllib module is imported and used for TOML parsing instead of the third-party tomli package.
On Python < 3.11, the third-party tomli package is imported (aliased as tomllib) and used for TOML parsing, preserving existing behavior.
TOML configuration files (e.g., pyproject.toml with [tool.pytest.ini_options]) are parsed identically regardless of which backend is selected.
Malformed TOML input raises TOMLDecodeError from the active backend, which is caught and re-raised as UsageError with the file path and error details.
The tomli package is no longer a required installation dependency when running on Python 3.11 or later.
acceptance_criteria: When running pytest on Python 3.11+ with a valid pyproject.toml containing [tool.pytest.ini_options], configuration is loaded successfully using the stdlib tomllib module without tomli installed.
When running pytest on Python < 3.11 with a valid pyproject.toml containing [tool.pytest.ini_options], configuration is loaded successfully using the tomli package.
When running pytest on Python 3.11+ with a malformed .toml file, a UsageError is raised containing the file path and parse error details.
When running pytest on Python < 3.11 with a malformed .toml file, a UsageError is raised containing the file path and parse error details, identical in structure to the Python 3.11+ case.
When inspecting the package metadata on Python >= 3.11, tomli does not appear as a required dependency.
When inspecting the package metadata on Python < 3.11, tomli remains listed as a required dependency.

task_11.title: Raise clear ValueError when empty tuple or falsy value is passed to pytest.raises()
task_11.description: Previously, passing an empty tuple `()` or other falsy value (e.g., `None`) to `pytest.raises()` as the expected exception would eventually produce a confusing, unhelpful error because no raised exception can ever be an instance of an empty set of types. The library now performs an early validation check and raises a descriptive `ValueError` immediately, guiding the user to understand that specifying no exception types is logically meaningless since any unhandled exception already fails the test.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `pytest.raises()` raises a clear, immediate error when the `expected_exception` argument is an empty tuple `()`, `None`, or any other falsy value, instead of producing a confusing error later in execution. The error message should explain why the input is invalid and clarify that raising exceptions is already understood as failing the test, so no special code is needed to say 'this should never raise an exception'.

expectation.grounded: When `pytest.raises()` is called with a falsy `expected_exception` value (including `()` or `None`), it must raise a `ValueError` before entering the context manager body or invoking the callable. The `ValueError` message must identify the invalid value passed and explain that it is impossible to match a raised exception against an empty set of types.
expectation.conceptual: When a user passes an empty or absent exception specification to `pytest.raises()`, the framework should fail fast with a clear, actionable error message rather than proceeding to produce a confusing failure downstream. The message should educate the user that no special assertion is needed to express 'this should never raise'.

constraints.grounded: Passing a single exception type or a non-empty tuple of exception types to `pytest.raises()` must continue to work exactly as before. The validation must only reject falsy values for `expected_exception`. The error raised must be `ValueError`, not `TypeError` or another exception class. Existing valid usages of `pytest.raises()` as both a context manager and a callable wrapper must not regress.
constraints.conceptual: The change must be purely additive in terms of input validation — all previously valid inputs must remain valid and behave identically. Only previously-broken or nonsensical inputs should now produce a better error. The fix must not alter the behavior of successful exception matching or the structure of the returned exception info.

behavior: Calling `pytest.raises(())` now raises `ValueError` immediately instead of producing a confusing error when the context manager block completes.
Calling `pytest.raises(None)` now raises `ValueError` immediately with a descriptive message.
Any other falsy value passed as `expected_exception` triggers the same early `ValueError`.
The `ValueError` message includes a repr of the invalid value passed and an explanation of why it is invalid.

Passing a valid exception type (e.g., `pytest.raises(ValueError)`) or a non-empty tuple of types (e.g., `pytest.raises((TypeError, ValueError))`) continues to work as before with no behavioral change.
acceptance_criteria: When `pytest.raises(())` is called, it should raise `ValueError` before any user code in the context manager body executes.
When `pytest.raises(None)` is called, it should raise `ValueError` with a message that includes the repr of the invalid value.
The `ValueError` message should explain that it is impossible to raise an exception matching an empty set of types and that no special code is needed to assert 'this should never raise'.
When `pytest.raises(SomeException)` is called with a valid exception type, behavior should be identical to the previous version.
When `pytest.raises((ExcA, ExcB))` is called with a non-empty tuple of valid types, behavior should be identical to the previous version.
The validation must occur at call time, not deferred to when an exception is actually raised or not raised.

task_10.title: Enhance error messages for pytest.warns() and ExceptionInfo.match() with multiline formatting
task_10.description: Improves the readability of failure messages produced by pytest.warns() and ExceptionInfo.match(). When pytest.warns() fails because no matching warning was emitted, the error output now uses pretty-printed multiline formatting for the list of emitted warnings, and displays the regex pattern and emitted warnings on separate labeled lines. Similarly, ExceptionInfo.match() now renders its assertion error in a structured multiline layout showing the regex and input value on distinct lines. These changes make it significantly easier to diagnose why a warning or exception match assertion failed, especially when dealing with long messages or large numbers of emitted warnings.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when pytest.warns() fails to match an expected warning (either by type or by regex), the resulting error message displays emitted warnings in a multiline, pretty-printed format rather than a single condensed line. Ensure that when ExceptionInfo.match() fails because a regex does not match the exception string, the error message presents the regex pattern and the input value on separate labeled lines for easy comparison.

expectation.grounded: When pytest.warns() raises a failure due to no warnings of the expected type being emitted, the 'DID NOT WARN' message must render the list of emitted warning messages using pformat-style multiline indented output. When pytest.warns() raises a failure due to no warnings matching the provided match regex, the error must display the regex and the emitted warnings on separate labeled lines ('Regex:' and 'Emitted warnings:'). When ExceptionInfo.match() raises an AssertionError because the regex did not match, the error message must use a multiline format with labeled lines for 'Regex:' and 'Input:'. The optional 're.escape()' hint must appear on its own line when the regex string is identical to the exception value string.
expectation.conceptual: Failure messages from pytest.warns() and ExceptionInfo.match() should use structured multiline formatting that clearly separates the expected pattern from the actual values, making it easy for users to visually compare and diagnose mismatches at a glance.

constraints.grounded: The conditions under which pytest.warns() and ExceptionInfo.match() raise failures must remain unchanged — only the formatting of the error messages is affected. pytest.warns() must still raise TypeError with the same semantic content when unexpected keyword arguments are passed. The match logic in WarningsChecker.__exit__() must still check issubclass(r.category, self.expected_warning) for type matching and re.search for regex matching. ExceptionInfo.match() must still return True on successful match and raise AssertionError on failure.
constraints.conceptual: No change in when or why failures are triggered. The matching semantics, success return values, and exception types raised must remain identical to the previous version. Only the human-readable content of the error messages changes.

behavior: When pytest.warns() fails because no warning of the expected type was emitted, the failure message now formats the list of emitted warning messages using pretty-print with multiline indentation instead of a flat single-line list representation.

When pytest.warns() fails because no warning matched the provided regex, the failure message now displays the regex pattern and emitted warnings on separate labeled lines rather than embedding them inline in a single sentence.
When ExceptionInfo.match() fails, the AssertionError message now shows 'Regex pattern did not match.' as a header followed by labeled 'Regex:' and 'Input:' lines, instead of a single-line format.
When ExceptionInfo.match() fails and the regex string is identical to the exception value string, the 're.escape()' hint is displayed on its own separate line.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest.warns(UserWarning) is used and no UserWarning is emitted but other warnings exist, the failure message should contain a newline-separated display of emitted warnings with indented formatting.

When pytest.warns(UserWarning, match='some_pattern') is used and warnings of the correct type exist but none match the regex, the failure message should display the regex on a line labeled 'Regex:' and the emitted warnings on a line labeled 'Emitted warnings:', each on separate lines.

When ExceptionInfo.match(r'some_pattern') is called and the regex does not match the exception string, the AssertionError should contain separate labeled lines for 'Regex:' and 'Input:' showing the pattern and exception value respectively.

When ExceptionInfo.match() is called with a pattern string that is identical to the exception's string value (suggesting the user forgot to escape regex metacharacters), the error message should include a 'Did you mean to re.escape()?' hint on its own line.
The conditions that trigger pytest.warns() failures (wrong warning type, no regex match) must remain unchanged from version 7.1.3.
ExceptionInfo.match() must still return True when the regex matches successfully.

task_14.title: Improve error message when no collector is found for a file
task_14.description: When pytest encounters a file for which no collector exists (e.g., a file with an unrecognized extension), the previous error message was cryptic, displaying an empty collectors list that provided no actionable information. This change differentiates between the case where collectors exist but the item is not found within them, and the case where no collectors are available at all, providing a clearer and more meaningful error message in the latter scenario.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when pytest is invoked with a file argument for which no collector can be found (e.g., an unrecognized file extension), the resulting error message clearly communicates the root cause rather than displaying a confusing internal representation such as an empty list of collectors.

expectation.grounded: When Session performs collection and encounters entries in _notfound where the collectors list is empty, the UsageError raised should contain the message 'found no collectors for <arg>' instead of the previous format 'not found: <arg> (no name <arg> in any of [])'. When the collectors list is non-empty (i.e., collectors exist but the name was not found within them), the error message should retain the existing format showing the argument and the list of collectors that were searched.
expectation.conceptual: When no collectors are available for a given file argument, pytest should display a concise, user-friendly error message indicating that no collectors were found. When collectors do exist but the item is absent from them, the error message should continue to list which collectors were searched.

constraints.grounded: The UsageError must still be raised with one error entry per not-found argument. The existing error format for the non-empty collectors case must remain unchanged to avoid breaking users who parse or match on that output. The branching logic must check the truthiness of the collectors list to distinguish the two cases.
constraints.conceptual: Existing error behavior for files that have matching collectors but are not found within them must not regress. The change must only affect the presentation of the error when there are genuinely no collectors available for the file type.

behavior: When pytest is run with a file argument that has no registered collector (e.g., an unrecognized extension), a UsageError is raised with the message 'found no collectors for <arg>' instead of the previous cryptic message containing an empty list.

When pytest is run with a file argument that has registered collectors but the name is not found in any of them, the existing error message format 'not found: <arg> (no name <arg> in any of <collectors>)' is preserved.
The error reporting loop iterates over all not-found entries and conditionally formats each message based on whether collectors were available for that entry.
acceptance_criteria: When running pytest with a file that has an unrecognized extension (e.g., 'something.unrecognized') and no collectors exist for it, the error output should contain 'found no collectors for something.unrecognized' and should not contain 'in any of []'.

When running pytest with a recognized file type argument that does not match any collected item but collectors do exist, the error output should still contain the original format showing which collectors were searched.
When multiple not-found arguments are provided with a mix of empty and non-empty collector scenarios, each argument should produce its appropriately formatted error message independently.
The UsageError exception should still be raised exactly once with all accumulated error messages when any not-found entries exist.

task_13.title: Display assertion messages without escaped newlines in verbose mode
task_13.description: When running pytest with very verbose mode (-vv), assertion error messages displayed escaped newline characters (literal '\n') in object representations, making large comparisons (e.g., dictionaries) difficult to read. The SafeRepr class and the saferepr function now accept a use_ascii parameter to control whether ascii() or the standard reprlib repr is used for object formatting. A new saferepr_unlimited function is introduced to produce unlimited-size safe repr strings, enabling the assertion display subsystem to render object representations with proper newlines instead of escaped sequences.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that assertion error messages displayed in very verbose mode (-vv) render object representations with actual newlines instead of escaped '\n' characters. Previously, the initial AssertionError line contained escaped newlines when comparing large objects (e.g., dictionaries with many keys), severely degrading readability of failure output.

expectation.grounded: The SafeRepr class accepts a use_ascii boolean parameter (default False) that controls whether ascii() is used instead of reprlib.Repr.repr() for object formatting. The saferepr function exposes the same use_ascii parameter. A new saferepr_unlimited function is available that returns an unlimited-size safe repr string with configurable ASCII mode (default use_ascii=True). When use_ascii is False, saferepr_unlimited falls back to repr(). Both saferepr_unlimited and SafeRepr.repr gracefully handle exceptions from failing __repr__ methods by returning formatted exception info.
expectation.conceptual: The safe repr subsystem provides control over whether object representations use ASCII-escaped output or standard repr output. An additional unlimited-size variant is available for contexts where truncation is undesirable, such as verbose assertion error display. Assertion failure messages in very verbose mode should render multi-line object representations with real newlines, not escaped newline sequences.

constraints.grounded: The default behavior of saferepr (with use_ascii=False and DEFAULT_REPR_MAX_SIZE) must remain unchanged to avoid regressions in non-verbose assertion output. SafeRepr must continue to catch and gracefully format exceptions from user-defined __repr__ methods. The saferepr_unlimited function must also catch exceptions and delegate to the existing _format_repr_exception helper. KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit must continue to propagate without being caught.
constraints.conceptual: Default assertion formatting behavior must not change for standard verbosity levels. Exception safety for objects with broken __repr__ implementations must be preserved across all repr functions. Critical system exceptions must never be silenced.

behavior: SafeRepr.__init__ accepts a new use_ascii boolean parameter (default False) that is stored as an instance attribute
SafeRepr.repr uses ascii(x) when use_ascii is True, and falls back to reprlib.Repr.repr(x) when use_ascii is False
saferepr passes the use_ascii parameter through to SafeRepr, defaulting to False
A new saferepr_unlimited function returns an unlimited-size safe repr string, defaulting to use_ascii=True
saferepr_unlimited catches exceptions from repr/ascii calls and returns formatted exception info via _format_repr_exception
When assertion errors are displayed in very verbose mode, object representations no longer contain escaped newline characters
acceptance_criteria: When a test fails with an assertion comparing large objects and pytest is run with -vv, the AssertionError line should display object representations with actual newlines, not escaped '\n' sequences
When saferepr is called with default parameters, the output should be identical to the behavior before this change (no regression)
When saferepr is called with use_ascii=True, the output should use ascii() representation for the object
When saferepr_unlimited is called on an object, the returned string should not be truncated regardless of object size
When saferepr_unlimited is called with use_ascii=True (default), it should return ascii() output for the object
When saferepr_unlimited is called with use_ascii=False, it should return repr() output for the object
When saferepr_unlimited is called on an object whose __repr__ raises an exception, it should return a formatted exception info string instead of propagating the error
When SafeRepr.repr encounters a KeyboardInterrupt or SystemExit, it should re-raise the exception without catching it

task_15.title: Add coloring to short test summary info
task_15.description: The short test summary section at the end of a pytest run now uses colored output to improve readability. Status words (FAILED, PASSED, ERROR, SKIPPED, XFAIL, XPASS) are rendered in their corresponding category colors, test name portions of node IDs are bolded, and the summary header itself is displayed in cyan bold. Additionally, xfailed reasons now appear on the same line as the test entry instead of on a separate indented line.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the short test summary info section uses colors to visually distinguish between different test result categories (failed, passed, error, skipped, xfailed, xpassed). Previously, the summary lines were uncolored plain text, making it difficult to scan and differentiate statuses at a glance, especially when multiple result types are intermixed.

expectation.grounded: The status keyword in each summary line (e.g., FAILED, PASSED, ERROR, SKIPPED, XFAIL, XPASS) must be rendered with ANSI color markup matching the color defined in `_color_for_type` for that result category, with a default fallback from `_color_for_type_default`. The test name portion of the node ID (everything after the first `::` separator) must be rendered in bold via `TerminalWriter.markup`. The `short test summary info` separator header must be rendered with cyan and bold attributes. For xfailed entries, the reason string must appear on the same line after a ` - ` separator rather than on a separate indented line. The `_get_line_with_reprcrash_message` function must accept a `TerminalWriter` instance and a `word_markup` dictionary instead of a raw terminal width integer.
expectation.conceptual: When a test run completes and the short test summary is displayed, each line should use color-coded status labels so users can instantly distinguish failures from skips, expected failures, passes, and errors. The test function name within each entry should be visually emphasized with bold styling. The summary section header should also be visually distinct. task_17.title: Display full crash messages in short test summary on CI
task_17.description: When pytest runs in a CI environment, crash messages shown in the short test summary info section are no longer truncated to the terminal width. Previously, all crash messages were trimmed based on terminal width, which caused useful diagnostic information to be lost in CI logs where terminal width constraints are irrelevant. Now, the full crash message is displayed when a CI environment is detected, while non-CI environments continue to trim messages to fit the terminal.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when pytest runs in a CI environment, the crash messages displayed in the 'short test summary info' section are shown in full without truncation. Previously, these messages were always trimmed to the terminal width, causing important failure context to be lost in CI log output where horizontal space is effectively unlimited.

expectation.grounded: The _get_line_with_reprcrash_message function must check running_on_ci() to determine truncation behavior. When running_on_ci() returns True, the reprcrash message must be appended to the summary line without any width-based trimming via _format_trimmed. When running_on_ci() returns False, the message must still be trimmed to fit within the TerminalWriter's fullwidth. The short test summary info output must reflect these behaviors for every FAILED, ERROR, or similarly flagged test entry.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest detects it is running in a CI environment, crash messages in the short test summary section should be displayed in their entirety. When not in CI, crash messages should continue to be truncated to fit the terminal width. This ensures CI logs contain full diagnostic information while interactive terminal output remains readable.

constraints.grounded: Non-CI environments must continue to truncate crash messages using _format_trimmed against the TerminalWriter's fullwidth. The running_on_ci() utility must be used for CI detection. The change must not affect other parts of the terminal output beyond the reprcrash message line in the short test summary. The msg-is-None guard after formatting must remain intact so that lines without a crash message are unaffected.
constraints.conceptual: The truncation behavior for non-CI environments must not regress. CI detection must rely on the existing CI-detection mechanism used elsewhere in pytest. Only the crash message portion of summary lines should be affected; other summary formatting must remain unchanged.

task_18.title: Support .pytest.ini as a hidden configuration file alternative
task_18.description: Pytest now recognizes .pytest.ini (dot-prefixed) as a valid configuration file, providing an alternative to pytest.ini. This allows users to keep their pytest configuration hidden using the Unix dot-file convention, consistent with other tools such as .flake8, .pylintrc, and .coveragerc. The new file is searched with higher priority than pyproject.toml, tox.ini, and setup.cfg, but lower priority than the existing pytest.ini.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest discovers and loads a hidden configuration file named .pytest.ini as an alternative to pytest.ini. Users should be able to use the Unix dot-file naming convention for their pytest configuration, aligning with the convention used by other development tools (.flake8, .pylintrc, .coveragerc, etc.).

expectation.grounded: The locate_config function must include .pytest.ini in the list of recognized configuration file names. When pytest searches for configuration, it should check for .pytest.ini after pytest.ini but before pyproject.toml, tox.ini, and setup.cfg. If .pytest.ini is found and no pytest.ini exists in the same directory, pytest should load configuration from .pytest.ini. The returned inifile and config dict should reflect the contents of .pytest.ini.
expectation.conceptual: When a user places a .pytest.ini file in their project, pytest should automatically discover and load it as configuration. The hidden dot-prefixed variant should behave identically to pytest.ini in terms of configuration parsing and option handling. If both pytest.ini and .pytest.ini exist, pytest.ini takes precedence.

constraints.grounded: Existing pytest.ini files must continue to be discovered and loaded exactly as before. The addition of .pytest.ini must not alter the resolution order or behavior for pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, tox.ini, or setup.cfg. When both pytest.ini and .pytest.ini exist in the same directory, pytest.ini must win due to its higher position in the search order.
constraints.conceptual: The change must be fully backward-compatible. Projects relying on any existing configuration file format must not experience any change in behavior. The hidden config file is purely an additive alternative and must not interfere with existing configuration discovery.

When neither pytest.ini nor .pytest.ini exists, pytest falls back to pyproject.toml, tox.ini, and setup.cfg in that order, unchanged from prior behavior.

When .pytest.ini defines custom markers or command-line defaults, those settings should be applied identically to how they would be applied from pytest.ini.

task_16.title: Normalize CLI help text to consistent sentence case and punctuation
task_16.description: All command-line option and ini-setting help descriptions in pytest were normalized to follow a consistent style: sentence case for the first word, trailing periods removed from single-sentence descriptions, multi-sentence descriptions ending each sentence with a period, 'Default is X' reformatted to 'Default: X.', and newline separators in help strings replaced with spaces. Group description labels (e.g. 'reporting' to 'Reporting') and environment variable descriptions displayed in --help output were also capitalized. Additionally, a new --no-showlocals CLI option was introduced to allow negating --showlocals when it is set via addopts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that all pytest command-line option help texts, ini-setting descriptions, option group labels, and environment variable descriptions displayed via `pytest --help` follow a consistent formatting convention: sentence case capitalization, no trailing period for single-sentence help strings, and a standardized 'Default: <value>.' format for default value documentation. Additionally, ensure that a --no-showlocals option exists to allow users to negate --showlocals when it has been set globally through addopts.

expectation.grounded: When `pytest --help` is invoked, every option help string produced by `pytest_addoption` across all built-in plugins (terminal, main, config, logging, capture, debugging, mark, doctest, cacheprovider, helpconfig, fixtures, python, junitxml, runner, assertion, stepwise, skipping, setuponly, setupplan, faulthandler, pastebin, pytester) must begin with an uppercase letter. Single-sentence help strings must not end with a period. Multi-sentence help strings must end each sentence with a period. Default value annotations must use the 'Default: <value>.' format rather than 'Default is <value>'. Option group descriptions (e.g. the 'Reporting' and 'Running and selection options' groups) must use sentence case. The environment variable descriptions for PYTEST_ADDOPTS, PYTEST_PLUGINS, PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD, and PYTEST_DEBUG must also use sentence case. The `--no-showlocals` option must be registered with `action='store_false'` on the `showlocals` dest, allowing it to override `--showlocals` when passed via addopts. The `Parser._anonymous` OptionGroup must use 'Custom options' as its label.
expectation.conceptual: Running `pytest --help` should display uniformly formatted help text for all options: each description starts with a capital letter, single sentences have no trailing period, multi-sentence descriptions are properly punctuated, and default values are shown in a consistent notation. A new --no-showlocals flag should be available to disable local variable display in tracebacks, specifically to counteract --showlocals when it is set in project-wide configuration.

constraints.grounded: No existing CLI option semantics, default values, choices, or dest attributes may be altered by this change. Only help string content, group description labels, and the addition of --no-showlocals are permitted. The --no-showlocals option must target the same 'showlocals' dest as --showlocals/--show-locals and use store_false action. No option names, short flags, or metavar values may change. The ini configuration key names must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The normalization must be purely cosmetic for all existing options — no change in runtime behavior, default values, or option parsing. The only functional addition is the new --no-showlocals flag. All previously valid CLI invocations must continue to work identically.
