task_19.title: Complete file-like interface on DontReadFromInput for captured stdin
task_19.description: When pytest capture is enabled, sys.stdin is replaced with a DontReadFromInput proxy object. This proxy was missing several standard file-like methods (readable, seekable, writable, flush, seek, tell, truncate, write, writelines), causing AttributeError when third-party code or the standard library introspected sys.stdin for the full IO interface (e.g., wrapping it with io.TextIOWrapper). The fix completes the file-like interface on DontReadFromInput so it conforms to the expected IO protocol, returning sensible defaults or raising UnsupportedOperation as appropriate.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that sys.stdin, when replaced by pytest's capture mechanism, implements the complete file-like object interface so that code relying on standard IO methods (such as readable(), seekable(), writable(), flush(), seek(), tell(), truncate(), write(), writelines()) does not raise AttributeError. Previously, wrapping sys.stdin.buffer with io.TextIOWrapper during capture would fail with 'DontReadFromInput object has no attribute readable'.

expectation.grounded: The DontReadFromInput class must implement the following additional methods to satisfy the IO base protocol: readable() returning False, seekable() returning False, writable() returning False, flush() raising UnsupportedOperation, seek() raising UnsupportedOperation, tell() raising UnsupportedOperation, truncate() raising UnsupportedOperation, write() raising UnsupportedOperation, and writelines() raising UnsupportedOperation. After this change, sys.stdin under capture mode must expose the same set of method names as a standard file-like object, preventing AttributeError on method access.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest capture is active, the stdin replacement object must behave as a well-formed file-like object. Introspection methods (readable, seekable, writable) must return False to indicate the stream is non-functional. Mutation and positioning methods (flush, seek, tell, truncate, write, writelines) must raise an appropriate unsupported-operation error rather than an AttributeError. Code that checks for or calls standard IO interface methods on sys.stdin during capture should never encounter a missing-attribute error.

constraints.grounded: The DontReadFromInput.read() and DontReadFromInput.readline() methods must continue to return empty results as before. The existing fileno() must continue to raise UnsupportedOperation. The isatty() method must continue to return False. The close() method must remain a no-op. The buffer property must continue to return self. No existing behavior of DontReadFromInput may be altered by this change.
constraints.conceptual: All previously existing behaviors of the captured stdin proxy must be preserved. The fix must only add missing interface methods without changing the semantics of existing ones. The proxy must not become readable, writable, or seekable — it must remain an inert placeholder that simply avoids AttributeError on standard method lookups.

task_20.title: Do not break into pdb on unittest.SkipTest during collection
task_20.description: When running pytest with the --pdb flag, a top-level `raise unittest.SkipTest()` in a test file (commonly used to skip entire modules based on platform or environment conditions) incorrectly triggered the pdb post-mortem debugger. This caused needless interactive breakpoints at skip statements, significantly disrupting developer workflow in projects with many conditionally-skipped test files. The fix ensures that unittest.SkipTest exceptions are excluded from pdb interaction, matching the existing expectation that skipped tests should not trigger the debugger.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when pytest is invoked with the --pdb flag, top-level `raise unittest.SkipTest()` statements in test files do not cause pytest to break into the pdb debugger. Previously, each such skip statement produced an unwanted interactive pdb breakpoint, forcing developers to manually continue past every skipped file. This was especially costly in large projects with many conditionally-skipped test modules.

expectation.grounded: When the PdbInvoke exception interaction hook processes an exception, it must check whether the exception value is an instance of unittest.SkipTest. If it is, the hook must skip invoking _enter_pdb entirely, allowing the skip to proceed silently. For all other exception types, pdb post-mortem behavior must remain unchanged. The isinstance check must target unittest.SkipTest specifically to avoid suppressing other exception types.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest is run with --pdb and a test file raises unittest.SkipTest at module level, pytest should skip the file silently without entering the debugger. The debugger should still activate for all genuine test failures and errors. Skipped tests should appear in the session summary as skipped, just as they do without the --pdb flag.

constraints.grounded: The pdb suppression must apply only to exceptions that are instances of unittest.SkipTest. All other exceptions, including subclasses of other skip-related types or generic exceptions, must continue to trigger pdb post-mortem as before. The pytest_internalerror handler must not be affected by this change. The existing behavior of _enter_pdb for non-skip exceptions must remain identical.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be narrowly scoped to unittest.SkipTest exceptions only. It must not suppress the debugger for any legitimate test failures, errors, or internal pytest errors. The overall --pdb experience for non-skip scenarios must be completely unaffected.

When --pdb is active and any non-SkipTest exception occurs, pdb post-mortem is invoked as before.
Skipped test files still appear in the session summary with the correct skip count and reason.
The pytest_internalerror path remains unchanged and continues to trigger pdb on internal errors.
The check is performed on the exception value stored in call.excinfo, using isinstance against unittest.SkipTest.
acceptance_criteria: When a test file contains a top-level `raise unittest.SkipTest('reason')` and pytest is run with --pdb, the debugger should NOT activate and the file should be reported as skipped.

task_21.title: Inherit pytest marks from all base classes using full MRO
task_21.description: Previously, when a test class used multiple inheritance, only markers from the first base class in the MRO were applied, silently dropping markers from other base classes. This fix changes mark resolution to traverse the full Method Resolution Order, collecting markers from all ancestor classes. Additionally, the ordering of inherited marks is corrected so that subclass marks precede superclass marks in MRO order (previously reversed), and the pytestmark attribute on a class now only stores marks directly applied to that class rather than accumulating inherited ones.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when a test class inherits from multiple base classes, each carrying distinct pytest markers, all markers from every base class in the MRO are collected and applied to the test class. Previously only markers from the first base class in the MRO were effective, causing markers from additional base classes to be silently lost. Ensure that marker ordering places subclass markers before superclass markers in MRO order. Ensure that the pytestmark attribute on a class only reflects marks directly applied to that class, not marks inherited from ancestors.

expectation.grounded: The get_unpacked_marks function, when called on a class type with consider_mro=True (the default), must iterate through the class's full __mro__ and collect pytestmark entries from each class in the chain. When consider_mro=False, it must only return marks from the class's own __dict__. The store_mark function must use consider_mro=False so that storing a new mark on a subclass does not flatten inherited marks into the subclass's pytestmark attribute. Node.iter_markers must yield marks from all ancestor classes, ordered with subclass marks first followed by superclass marks in MRO order.
expectation.conceptual: When resolving markers for a test class in a multiple-inheritance hierarchy, the framework must collect markers from all base classes, not just the first one. Markers must be ordered so that the most specific class's markers appear first, followed by ancestor markers in standard Python MRO order. Directly querying a class's marker attribute must return only that class's own markers, while the standard marker iteration API aggregates the full inheritance chain.

constraints.grounded: The get_unpacked_marks function must continue to handle non-class objects (e.g., functions, modules) by reading the pytestmark attribute via getattr without MRO traversal. The consider_mro parameter must default to True to preserve backward-compatible behavior for callers that do not pass the argument. The normalize_mark_list pipeline must still be applied to all collected marks. The store_mark function must not accumulate inherited marks into the subclass's pytestmark list, to prevent duplication upon repeated mark storage.
constraints.conceptual: Non-class objects such as test functions and modules must continue to have their markers resolved exactly as before, with no behavioral change. The default behavior of mark collection must include full MRO traversal so existing call sites are unaffected. Marks must still be normalized and validated. Storing a new mark on a class must not cause inherited marks to be duplicated or incorrectly persisted onto the subclass.

behavior: When a test class inherits from two or more marked base classes, markers from all base classes are now collected instead of only from the first base class in the MRO.
Inherited marks are ordered with the subclass's own marks first, followed by marks from each superclass in MRO order (previously the order was reversed).
The pytestmark attribute on a class now contains only the marks directly applied to that class; previously it accumulated marks from all ancestor classes.
The get_unpacked_marks function accepts a consider_mro keyword argument: when True (default) it traverses the full MRO for class objects; when False it reads only the class's own __dict__.
The store_mark function now calls get_unpacked_marks with consider_mro=False to avoid flattening inherited marks into the subclass's pytestmark attribute.
For non-class objects (functions, modules), mark resolution behavior is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given a test class that inherits from two base classes each decorated with a distinct marker, when markers are resolved for the test class, then both base class markers are present.

task_22.title: Display inner exceptions of ExceptionGroups in pytest output
task_22.description: pytest previously suppressed or failed to render inner exceptions contained within PEP-654 BaseExceptionGroup instances when using non-native traceback display styles (e.g., --tb=short, --tb=long). This change forces a fallback to native traceback rendering for BaseExceptionGroup exceptions so that all nested sub-exceptions become visible in test output, regardless of the chosen traceback style. It also adds compatibility with Python versions below 3.11 by importing BaseExceptionGroup from the exceptiongroup backport package when needed. This is an interim measure pending full pytest-native rendering support for exception groups.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when a test raises a BaseExceptionGroup (PEP-654), all inner/nested exceptions within the group are fully displayed in the pytest test output, regardless of the active traceback display style (--tb=short, --tb=long, --tb=line, etc.). Previously, inner exceptions were silently omitted or collapsed when a non-native traceback style was selected, causing users to lose critical diagnostic information about multiple simultaneous failures.

expectation.grounded: When FormattedExcinfo encounters a BaseExceptionGroup during exception chain traversal, it must produce a ReprTracebackNative representation using Python's standard traceback.format_exception, bypassing the styled repr_traceback path. On Python < 3.11, BaseExceptionGroup must be resolved from the exceptiongroup backport package. For all other (non-ExceptionGroup) exceptions, the existing styled repr_traceback behavior must remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: When a test raises an ExceptionGroup containing multiple nested exceptions, pytest must render the full tree of inner exceptions in the test failure output. This must work consistently across all traceback display modes, not only the native mode. The feature must be compatible with both Python 3.11+ (built-in ExceptionGroup) and earlier Python versions using the exceptiongroup backport.

constraints.grounded: Non-ExceptionGroup exceptions must continue to be formatted through the existing repr_traceback method with no behavioral change. The BaseExceptionGroup detection must use isinstance checking. The native fallback must only apply to BaseExceptionGroup instances, not to arbitrary exception types. The exceptiongroup backport import must be conditional on Python version < 3.11 and must not affect Python 3.11+ environments where BaseExceptionGroup is a builtin.
constraints.conceptual: The rendering of standard (non-grouped) exceptions must not be altered. The fallback to native display is a temporary measure and must not preclude a future full implementation of styled exception group rendering. Cross-version compatibility must be maintained without introducing unconditional new dependencies for Python 3.11+ users.

behavior: When a BaseExceptionGroup is encountered during exception representation, pytest switches to native traceback formatting for that exception, displaying the full exception tree including all nested sub-exceptions.
When a non-ExceptionGroup exception is encountered, pytest continues to use the user-selected traceback style (short, long, line, etc.) with no change in behavior.
On Python < 3.11, BaseExceptionGroup is imported from the exceptiongroup backport package to enable detection and proper rendering.
On Python >= 3.11, the built-in BaseExceptionGroup is used directly without requiring any backport import.

task_23.title: Fix caplog.get_records() returning stale data after caplog.clear()
